claims.claim_text: The indexed Joseph R. Hayden is University of Michigan political scientist Joseph Ralston Hayden, an early COI recruit.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Joseph Hayden, a University of Michigan political scientist and former vice governor of the Philippines
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS and Michigan align on name, university, profession, Philippine office, and 1941-1945 COI/OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; two authoritative institutions provide several unusually specific identifiers beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: Michigan dates his COI/OSS work from 1941 to 1945 after his 1935 return to the university.
claims.match_notes: The Box 320 file remains unreviewed. The expanded middle name is supplied by the University of Michigan finding aid.

claims.claim_text: Joseph Hayden's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the University of Michigan political science department.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Following his return, Hayden was named James Orin Murfin Professor of Political Science and chairman of the department.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Michigan documents his university return and faculty leadership, then dates his COI/OSS service from 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; university, profession, Philippine service, and exact wartime chronology align with NPS.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded: faculty employment preceded the 1941 COI assignment.
claims.match_notes: No intervening civilian or military affiliation is documented in the authoritative sources reviewed.

claims.claim_text: Joseph Hayden's last documented civilian employer before COI/OSS service was the University of Michigan.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The university finding aid gives a continuous faculty chronology from 1935 to his wartime federal service beginning in 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the institutional biography and official OSS history describe the same distinctive career.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded immediately before federal wartime service.
claims.match_notes: The university employer is distinct from Hayden's later COI, OSS, and War Department assignments.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Wilmarth S. Lewis is Yale graduate and Horace Walpole scholar Wilmarth Sheldon Lewis, who worked for OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Mr. Lewis worked at the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name, Yale class, Walpole specialization, Farmington base, and OSS service align across Yale and NPS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; two authoritative sources provide a uniquely specific name, specialty, and wartime assignment.
claims.temporal_assessment: Yale places several Washington OSS years within a lifelong Farmington-based collecting and editorial career.
claims.match_notes: The Box 451 file remains unreviewed; the indexed P-7 grade is consistent with civilian personnel.

claims.claim_text: Wilmarth Lewis's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation was independent Horace Walpole scholarship, editing, and collecting.
claims.evidence_excerpt: devoted his life to creating the world's greatest collection relating to Horace Walpole
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Yale describes the lifelong independent project; NPS identifies him as a Horace Walpole biographer among the early COI recruits.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, Yale association, subject specialization, and OSS chronology align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded before the Washington OSS interval, though the scholarship later resumed and continued.
claims.match_notes: This is a professional affiliation, not Yale employment and not an assertion of paid self-employment. No reliable named pre-OSS employer has yet been identified.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Junius S. Morgan is the J.P. Morgan & Co. banker and U.S. Naval Reserve officer assigned to OSS financial control.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS names Junius S. Morgan of J.P. Morgan & Co. in the OSS financial group; the official Navy register matches the private index number.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact distinctive name, banking firm, OSS function, Navy rank, and an exact private number match align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1944 register documents his Navy commander status during the OSS period; NPS documents his OSS financial assignment.
claims.match_notes: The Army classification generated from the bare index rank has been corrected to commissioned naval officer using the official register. The full number remains private.

claims.claim_text: Junius Morgan's last identified civilian employer before wartime Navy and OSS service was J.P. Morgan & Co.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Junius S. Morgan of J.P. Morgan and Company in New York
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official NPS history identifies the banker by firm when explaining his selection for OSS financial control.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, employer, OSS role, rank, and private number match align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the civilian affiliation from which his wartime financial expertise was drawn; the exact departure date is not stated.
claims.match_notes: The available sources do not securely establish whether Naval Reserve duty or bank employment was the immediate predecessor to the OSS assignment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Colonel William L. Rehm is William Lane Rehm, the OSS finance officer identified by NPS as W. Lane Rehm.
claims.evidence_excerpt: W. Lane Rehm, financial genius of one of the largest investment trusts in the United States
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index rank and middle initial, NPS name and specialized OSS role, and University of Chicago full name align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the uncommon surname, Lane middle name, colonel rank, finance background, and distinctive OSS function corroborate one another.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS places Rehm in the OSS unvouchered-funds group; the university source establishes the expanded name but not employment chronology.
claims.match_notes: The Box 637 file remains unreviewed. The private service number is masked and is not needed for the public identity statement.

claims.claim_text: Before OSS, William Lane Rehm had senior financial experience with a large U.S. investment trust whose name is not given in the accessible official source.
claims.evidence_excerpt: financial genius of one of the largest investment trusts in the United States
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS describes the financial background that led to Rehm's placement in the three-person OSS unvouchered-funds group.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; name variants, colonel rank, finance specialty, and OSS fiscal responsibility align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented as pre-OSS professional background, but neither the institution's name nor the exact sequence into OSS is stated.
claims.match_notes: No employer is invented from weaker biographies. The personnel file is needed to identify the investment trust and establish dates.

claims.claim_text: The initials-only indexed R. H. Goddard is Robert H. Ives Goddard, the Providence financier assigned to OSS financial control.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Robert H. Ives Goddard, an immensely wealthy financier from Providence, Rhode Island
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS supplies the full name, Providence location, occupation, and OSS role; the 1941 directory independently supplies the same name, city, and finance-related firms.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the official OSS role plus Providence, exact initials, expanded Ives name, and contemporary corporate affiliations provide multiple corroborating identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: The directory is contemporaneous with COI creation in 1941; NPS places the same person in the OSS financial group.
claims.match_notes: The expansion is documented and displayed as a variant; the original initials-only index form remains visible. Box 278 remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: Robert H. Ives Goddard's best-supported immediate pre-OSS institutional affiliation was Goddard Brothers in Providence.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Goddard Bros (R H Ives Goddard, Wm Gammell jr) agts cotton gds mfg companies
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 1941 directory names Goddard in the firm's listing and personal entry; NPS identifies the Providence financier in OSS financial control.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; name, city, finance and corporate roles, and OSS function align across a contemporary directory and official history.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded in the 1941 directory, the year COI was established.
claims.match_notes: This is presented as professional affiliation, not as a salaried employer. His concurrent trusteeships and land-company presidencies remain documented in the citation notes.
